text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Weakening of Dutch guilder against German mark puts pressure on Dutch central bank to raise interest rates. (p1)
- Dutch government has been ignoring bourse rules for listing of state bonds since 1983. (p1)
- Publisher Reed Elsevier takes over medical publisher Bugamor. (p1)
- Alitalia chief says KLM would be his preferred alliance partner. (p1)
- ING Investment Management's growth in first half of 1997 is fuelled by group's insurance arm. (p7) DE VOLKSKRANT
- Advertisers association VEA expects businesses to spend even less on advertising in 1997 than they did last year. (p2)
- Entrepreneur buys some assets of bankrupt aircraft maker Fokker. (p2)
- KLM partner Eurowings crosses one million passenger mark for first time in its 20-year existence. (p2) DE TELEGRAAF
- Accelerated construction of Schiphol airport's fifth runway would make it unnecessary to levy environmental surcharge on air tickets to pay for sound-proofing of homes. (p1)
- Economic affairs minister Hans Wijers denies he is in running to take over as head of PTT Telecom. (p2)
- Bank insurer Fortis says it was not sorry to see 20-strong team of East Europe specialists move to rival ABN Amro Bank. (21)
- Some two billion guilders' worth of 1,000 guilder notes disappear each year to banks abroad, according to report by government's Central Planning Bureau. (p1)
- Paper and packaging concern KNP BT continues long search for a partner for its paper-making unit KNP Leykam. (p9)
